title: Anthropic explains how Claude’s invisible text watermarks will work
slides: Can Claude's watermark survive heavy editing?
Anthropic embeds invisible patterns into generated text.
The signal persists even after translation or paraphrasing.
Detectable only by Anthropic's API, not by humans.
Run your own text through their detector now.
thread_text:
1. The invisible edit test

Anthropic’s watermark survives translation and paraphrasing, even after heavy editing.

2. Why watermarks matter now

It’s a response to deepfakes and misinformation, but the trade-off is privacy vs. provenance.

3. Who controls the verdict

Only Anthropic’s API can detect it—so platforms could gatekeep or censor content.

4. A silent shift in trust

You’ll never know if a text you read was AI-generated unless someone runs the check.

5. Try it on your own work

Run a recent post through their detector. Would you want that result public?

instagram.caption:
Your text can be translated, paraphrased, and heavily edited—and Anthropic can still tell it was written by Claude.  

The company embeds invisible patterns into generated text. Only their API can detect the signal, not human readers. This is their answer to deepfakes, but it hands platforms a private verification tool.  

If you publish AI-assisted work, a third party could now verify it without telling you 🤖. You’d never know if your post was flagged unless they choose to show you.  

Would you publish a text knowing a silent check could label it later? Try running one of your old posts through their detector—do you want that result public 🔍?
